rule: Runbook criterion 11: every slice has a recorded verify-<slice> verdict; no barrier is crossed with an open NOT DISCHARGED; and every 'behaviour the commit bodies do not mention' finding is either documented or reverted. R-35's mechanism was real and used throughout the campaign -- commit bodies across the range cite verify-P2b and verify-P5-retire findings and answer six NOT DISCHARGED verdicts by name -- but the verdicts themselves were only ever written into commit bodies, so 'every slice has a recorded verdict' could not be checked from the repository. That is the first half of the criterion and it is the half this file exists to start.
what_this_ledger_does_not_hold: The verdicts of the campaign's earlier slices. They are recoverable only by reading the commit bodies that answer them, one range at a time, and reconstructing them here from those bodies would be this campaign's own failure shape -- a record derived from the thing it is supposed to check independently. So the ledger starts where a lane could record a verdict honestly, which is the pass that produced it, and the gap for everything before it is stated rather than papered over. A campaign that ran this file from slice one would have the criterion; this one has the mechanism and one pass.

criteria.what_was_found: Production emission: every disposition on every payload is MEASURED and OutcomeLedger had no construction site in src/. Second clause: 'static/js/app.js takes exactly one budgeted change at S9' is false -- three commits touched it.
criteria.note: The construction-site half is closed and the ledger is filled by every real fight. The emission half is blocked on an adjudication ruling, now named and its footprint measured. The app.js clause is recorded as gap G10 of the campaign-close report; reverting a shipped refactor to satisfy a budget clause would be worse than recording the overrun.

criteria.note: The scan is mechanised and the residue is pinned as a number, so a further site fails a gate. The criterion's wording stays unmet and the report says so.

criteria.note: Each row now names its dependent criterion and states how it is read under the deferral, in H5's shape. Nothing is answered; an implementation lane may not answer an [H].

criteria.note: The plans half was already green and machine-gated; the receipts and commit-body half now is too.

No committed ledger of per-slice verdicts, so 'every slice has a recorded verdict' cannot be checked from the repository; and the closing barrier was being crossed with open NOT DISCHARGED verdicts.
criteria.note: This file is the mechanism the criterion's first half needs, carrying one pass. Its second half -- no barrier crossed with an open NOT DISCHARGED -- is not met and cannot be by a lane: three clauses stay open and two of the three need an umbrella ruling. The third half is met: every unmentioned-behaviour finding below is documented, none reverted.

unmentioned_behaviour.note: Both re-verified against data/ directly and filed as dated, gated entries with reproducers. Neither reaches a damage number and the gate asserts it.

unmentioned_behaviour.note: Recorded in that commit's body: a commit body cannot be amended, and the receipt's own scope-and-limits block is the authority on the verdict's strength.

unmentioned_behaviour.note: The family scan is derived from filenames and does fail on a new family with a standing dissent -- but only if the dissent is ordered, and an unreadable date was what made one unorderable. The same hole as the first finding.

unmentioned_behaviour.note: Gap G10 of the campaign-close report, with the three commits and their line counts.

coverage.rule: Runbook criterion 11's first clause -- every slice has a recorded verify-<slice> verdict -- had no denominator. 'Every slice' bounded nothing a machine could read, so a ledger holding one pass and a ledger holding forty were indistinguishable to every gate. This block is the denominator, derived from the tree rather than authored: the campaign's own slice labels, which are the trailing parenthetical tag each lane stamped on its commit subjects.
coverage.how_the_population_is_derived: The first element of the trailing parenthetical of every commit subject in 584071e..HEAD. A commit whose subject carries no such tag is counted in untagged_commits and reported rather than dropped -- a slice that never labelled itself is a hole in the convention, not an absence of slices.
coverage.what_this_block_does_not_do: It does not reconstruct a verdict. The earlier passes' verdicts live only in the commit bodies that answer them, and rebuilding them here from those bodies would be a record derived from the thing it is supposed to check independently -- the reason the ledger began mid-campaign. What is recorded is whether a slice group has a verdict IN THIS LEDGER, which is a fact about this file and is checkable without reading a single body.
coverage.what_the_residue_buys: Two things the criterion never had. The gap is a number that cannot grow in silence, the way the sole-home scan made criterion 4's residue a number. And the gate asserts the derived tag set equals these two lists -- so the NEXT slice group cannot ship without either a verdict row or an explicit line in slice_groups_without_one. Going forward the clause holds by machine; backwards it is measured and open, which is the honest pair.
coverage.why_the_residue_cannot_be_closed_retroac: A verify verdict is a fresh read-only agent's report on a tree at a commit. The trees are still there and the agents are not, and a verdict written now by anyone who has read the plan is not an R-35 verdict at all -- the brief's whole content is that the reader has not read the plan. So the residue closes by the campaign ending, or by re-running R-35 over the historical ranges as its own scheduled work with its own briefs. It does not close by anybody filling in this file.
